steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: Huff, huff... *cough*...

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: You're here again... Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Look, miss! I drew you something!

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: Ha, I can hear you drawing something on the quarantine cabin walls... Amiya.

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: But I can't see anymore... I've been blind since yesterday.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh, I know! I'll come in—

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: Don't. I might just—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's alright, Miss. I'm Infected too, remember? Babel's doctors are close, so I'm sure they'll take good care of us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Miss, give me your hand, and I'll draw it out for you!
The tiny Cautus gently takes the hand of the Infected patient lying on the sickbed into her own—Black crystals cover her entire body, an enchanting Originite sheen circulating inside the crystals.
Amiya knows what this means for an Infected. She has seen it before.
Her finger earnestly traces a shape on the patient's palm.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You said the name you got from your parents is a flower you've never seen.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I went to ask the Doctor and Theresa about it, and they brought me to see the real thing!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Can you feel it, Miss? I'm drawing it on your palm with my finger.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Your name is so pretty!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Um, was my drawing too messy? I can try again...

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: Little bunny... Aren't you scared of me?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Huh? Why would I be scared of you?

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: We've just recently arrived at Babel, but I'm fond of you, Amiya.

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: We're friends, right...? Can you help a friend out? Help me ring a doctor with the bell.

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: I'd like them to bring me to see... no, to touch those flowers.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...I want to go with you too.

steps.name: Dying Infected
steps.text: No can do. You're sick as well, so be good and stay here.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Then I'll wait for you to come back.
The Infected patient says nothing, and only rubs Amiya's head.
Amiya sees the patient trying her best to bear the pain, and the shiny Originium crystals on her arm.
Amiya, you had just followed the Doctor to Babel then.
I still remember you sat at the door of the quarantine cabin for a long time, persistently refusing to move.
The Doctor found you in silence, and sat down to join you. You only started crying when the Doctor hugged you.
I too, wanted to hold you in my arms, but I couldn't bear to disturb you both.
Amiya... you're a bright child. You knew that Infected would never return.
She didn't want you to see her leave. It would be too cruel for a child to witness. But she didn't know just how strong you are.
I see many things from your gentle eyes. You want to help them...
No matter their race or Infection status—you see them all as lively, lovely people.
It was from that moment I began to harbor a selfish idea—
Perhaps... you could bear this crown in the future...
Perhaps... you can go further than I have.
I was in no hurry to hand over a responsibility this heavy to you. I thought I had the luxury of time to be by your side as you grew up—
I'm sorry, Amiya. I broke my promise.

options: ...The Arts that trapped us in there is gone.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa's aura... is fading away.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, Dr. Kal'tsit... is it over?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm sorry, Doctor... I didn't find any leads to the primordial Originium from Theresa.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We were one step too late.

options: The first Originium has been sent away.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So you've noticed, Doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Can you still see the top of the spire now?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, aren't we standing on...

options: ...Those huge white pillars are still extending downwards...
I can no longer see where they end...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm afraid the dust isn't going to settle so easily.
These threads are such an eyesore—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There she is!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Bunny! Help me out!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Everyone's saying she's gone, but I have to see it for myself.
Pink-white threads fork out like branches, attaching and growing on the white pillars.
They land on the red roots, wrapping, twisting...
Eventually covering this tower of infinity completely.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Amiya, I'm not going to regret like I did back then again.

steps.name: W
steps.text: At the very least, I hope this time...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The same goes for us.
Amiya walks to the silk-wrapped roots, gently touching the soft matter.
Sparks of flame drop from the hem of her skirt, leaving clusters of fire in her path.
The flames under her do not extinguish easily, but spread to the threads.
They continue to climb, replacing the fractured white threads as they wrap around the only tower standing between land and sky.
Threads flutter and fall to the floor.
They quickly cover the roots, like a garden in bloom by wind, with flames burning within.
Theresa sits among the flower-like flames, leaning on the roots as she looks at the golden ocean in the 'sky' coming to a calm.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya, you're so much stronger than I imagined. How warm these flames are...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'Flames that burn away all decay', you've really done it, Amiya.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Well, since that's done, come over. Closer.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa, we—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Ssh... I know what you're thinking in that little mind of yours.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Look at the ocean above our heads. The waves we made are calming down. Soon we'll leave.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya. Some wishes shouldn't be voiced out loud, because they'll only leave more sorrow behind.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, Theresa. I don't want to leave any more regrets. I wish... we all wish you can stay.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Even if I'll let you all down again?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Isn't it more important to have the people I care about know how I feel? That's what the Doctor taught me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: *smiles* You've truly grown up, Amiya.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...I'll always be with you, Amiya. As I promised you...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Originium no longer contains the slightest bit of my own information, but I'm sure you won't abandon the ideals I once hoped for.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Is there no other way to let you stay—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: To save me, and end this war?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There is no one on this land that will manage to realize every single wish. That includes even the creator.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya, do not lament over the dead. Exercise more concern for the living, especially those who scoff at the notion of hope.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But for now, before we leave... let's quietly—

steps.name: W
steps.text: Your Highness! Sorry, I-I just, couldn't keep it in anymore.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh... W? Is this a hug from you?

steps.name: W
steps.text: Your Highness...? Your eyes...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I can't see clearly anymore. The information flow holding this body together is fading away.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But I still have my sense of touch. And I can tell you're not crying. That's good.
Theresa reaches out and returns the embrace, gently patting W's shoulder.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Your Highness, y-you don't mind...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Why would I?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hm... I suppose worrying about that isn't anything strange coming from you. You haven't changed one bit, W.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I can still remember our time back at Babel, when you were hiding in a corner with your camera in hand, hesitating to come forward...

steps.name: W
steps.text: ...Y-You saw me?!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Of course. Actually, I was even waiting for you to come over for a photo together. But you never did manage to muster up the courage.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Your Highness?! You saw—and even remembered that?!

steps.name: W
steps.text: E-Even—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Taking a cheeky picture of me? Not just that. I didn't think the reckless mercenary from back then would grow into the woman before me today.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The truth of how the Chernobog and Lungmen conflicts were actually settled, the mercenary group giving Manfred headaches for the past few years, and of course, your appearance in this place that shouldn't have happened at all...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You can achieve so much more than you imagine, W.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You should have realized by now I'm not so divine as you believe, and you're not insignificant.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Haha... Hahaha! I don't care if you're consoling me, or deceiving me—I'm taking it to heart!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Your Highness, you really are always so... gentle. When we first arrived in this damn place, when I saw you, I was so afraid—

steps.name: W
steps.text: I want to make up for that missed photo opportunity, Your Highness!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Camera, camera... wait, when did it break—That damn Qalid'čoa!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm afraid it wouldn't work here, even if it wasn't broken.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: W, I know you don't want to leave any regrets. I am the same.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I don't want to leave you thinking I break my promises.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Wha?!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I still owe you a name, remember?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'W' belongs to a departed Sarkaz, and a cycle that should have ended...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: As I said, you deserve a more fitting name. A proper name for a Sarkaz woman like yourself.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Well, I did want to wait until the dust settled in Kazdel first, but I'm afraid I won't get to see that day come.

steps.name: W
steps.text: Wait, Your Highness! Hold on, I, I... still don't get...

steps.name: W
steps.text: Give me some time! Wait, no! I should be writing this down!

steps.name: W
steps.text: Screw it, I don't care anymore! I'm ready!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'Wiš'adel'.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...Will that be hard to remember?

steps.name: W
steps.text: How could it be?

steps.name: W
steps.text: 'Wiš'a', and 'del', right? Del means home, that I know. But Wi... wiš'a...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It means to 'Wish'.

steps.name: W
steps.text: To wish... for a home.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes. Kazdel's destiny—could you witness it, in my stead?

steps.name: W
steps.text: But... I... you... Theresis...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kazdel's future is in your hands. Not mine, nor Theresis's.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You'll understand when the day comes.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Haha... Alright! Wiš'adel... Wiš'a—del...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: It's engraved onto my brain forever. I'll never forget it!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I like it. Sounds so much better than the names Hoederer threw at me from his dictionary.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Kal'tsit, Amiya, and you in the hood. Heard that? Call me Wiš'adel from now on. And you'd better not get it wrong.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Also, I just decided to head down to the Military Commission later and bomb my name out with explosives. That way, nobody'll ever forget it.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Or maybe the roof's better. I want the flames to spread so far you can even see it from Londinium...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wiš'a...del.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I know what you want to say. I'm not crying.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I'm shaking because... hehe... hah...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: *ahem* Why's everyone all quiet now?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You.. I... can't find the words to say...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Go, Amiya.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Before she vanishes completely... she'll be happy with you by her side.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even if she'll never admit it herself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, we may be standing against Theresa now, but I have to admit she has achieved something beyond the limits of my imagination.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I believe you as you are right now, should already have some conjectures in mind even if you're missing your past memories.

options: It has something to do with that mysterious person.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresa, our mission is far from being over, yes?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Have you already handed the first Originium to him?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Theresa, this difficult problem you're leaving us with is truly—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kal'tsit, things don't always go the way we want. All we have done is to do what we should, nothing more.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor, your appearance before me right now is proof I've won our earlier bet.

options: You still hide so many secrets.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hah. Doctor, allow me to instill a little bit more suspense.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You're still not ready, even now, even if all of you've surpassed me—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: See the ocean waves billowing?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We don't have much time left.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I always knew our reunion only meant another parting.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: My dear Kal'tsit, since we're all clear about our respective endings, why should we go through sorrow yet again?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Can you come closer?
Theresa stretches out her hand and touches the ends of Kal'tsit's hair.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Ah, here you are. I hope my staunch and strong Kal'tsit isn't shedding any tears this time either.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're always like this.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm a very fortunate soul, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Every time I leave, I do so with my dearest friend by my side...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa... she's disappearing...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: She's what? Bunny, what kinda nonsense is that? Isn't Her Highness with us right now? I'm even hugging—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Wiš'adel, haven't you achieved what you wanted to do...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You met, defeated me, and finally, killed me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It's time to let go.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I will leave without a trace, and no longer exist anywhere you can see.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresa, do you mean that the Originium will no longer bear any traces of you?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes, I won't allow Originium to become our cage.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: All that I've strived for, is just to free the Sarkaz completely.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Sarkaz should be free, in both life and death.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'Destroy something, to create a ladder...' Even if what I end up destroying is myself.

options: You're so... different from the Theresa I had in mind.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}... This is our 'first' meeting, isn't it?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What bits have you heard of me... what kind of Theresa do you have in your mind?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A founder of Babel, a faultless idealist?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Or a cold, calculated King of Sarkaz, a schemer who instigates war?

options: Both are roles that others need you to play.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Is that so...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I didn't think we'd get the chance to say our farewells so peacefully.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A friend bid farewell to me here, a long time ago.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I witnessed my friend's death, and from here I began walking towards my own.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: ...I like this place.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But it is also somewhere I cannot reach or visit, ever.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It only perpetually exists in the memories of the void, unreachable throughout my whole life.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, what kind of person do I seem to you right now—?

options: Someone who would do everything and anything for the fate of their people.
Someone always chasing after a lofty ideal.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Is that so? Quite the interesting answer.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You and me, past and present, what is gone, and what is to come...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Time seems to hold no meaning here. Perhaps we have already said something similar at some other point in time.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But what you say isn't completely baseless.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I was once warned about my future, but I was clear this was my path to tread.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I wouldn't give up, no matter if I lived or died, regardless of place and time.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: However, the very same words coming from you hold no irony at all.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Thank you, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What defines a lofty ideal? Who ought to define it?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I exacted violence on other races for Sarkaz freedom. I renounced the belief I once defended with my life, and stood against all of you...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Rhodes Island of today has already stepped out of Babel's shadow...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Though it has abandoned some concepts Babel once adhered to, for the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You fly peace as your banner, but employ violence to help our oppressors bring back suffering to the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But at the same time, I can't deny your own lofty ideals, just like how I can't deny my past self.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Perhaps you believe you completely comprehend what 'lofty' means... but for me, the phrase still weighs too heavy.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: However, thank you, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I can sense you're not lying right now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But if you're still going to give a perfunctory reply at such a moment... my disappointment will only grow.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Of course, a little loss isn't surprising at all. I really want to know your answer, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor, don't give up on finding the answer. If you're still just following Rhodes Island's ideals as you go—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I worry if you're ready enough to handle whatever it is that you encounter in the future.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Just keep going, like how I hoped you would in the past.

options: ...To be honest, I can't give you a proper evaluation.
You're still a conundrum to me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You're cautious, still hostile and wary toward me just like you were back then... of course, we stand now on opposing sides like we did before.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But no matter. You merely haven't had enough time to figure out each and every single enigma there is.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A pity we always have our chats when the clock is ticking down so fast.

options: I heard so many stories about you on Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: My mission is over.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Many years ago, you and Kal'tsit pushed a door open for me, to a wider world.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But I was already a sovereign to the Sarkaz. I bear their suffering, their fate.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: My ideals and vision may transcend that sky of nothingness, but the weight of reality still pulled me back down to earth.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I was already convinced back then that the person who could change the Sarkaz, or even the future of Terra itself was absolutely not me—it has never been me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A close friend whom I trust the most already predicted this end.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor, give me your hand.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes, I had the fortune to meet your 'truest' self.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That person was wise, gentle.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Though bearing with the heaviest of duty and wearing the strongest of shackles, that one never gave up hope, ever.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'm gratified.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You stand alongside Kal'tsit and Amiya now, and so I believe I made the right choice back then.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The choices we made on our own have also determined the path to where we are now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Our original meeting in haste was just like this parting between two strangers... was it not?

options: I can't sense any... resentment from you.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Resentment? Why?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: To this day, I still feel only regret and a longing from when I touched the depths on your soul and the unimaginable truth.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes... it is because I touched the depths of your heart that I hold so much regret... we lost a chance to walk on the same path.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Perhaps that person was so fascinating due to an internal conflict no one else can empathize with.

options: ...Speculations, questions—I can't piece together fully what 'I' was.
All this contradictory information is making me feel confused and anxious.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Haven't you noticed? You don't doubt your decisions now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What shapes your true self? Everything that you've experienced, or your already concealed past?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Look at where we are, Doctor.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Those silent memories and the truth of everything, are they not by your side...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Past, present, future. Time is no longer defined by the rules we find so familiar at the end of Originium.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You no longer remember...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But you told me once, that 'Originium'—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Brought an innumerable amount of suffering upon this land, along with countless possibilities. Created by hundreds of millions of sacrifices in the era you came from.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: When you created Originium, what expectations did you harbor towards it and this land?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Look, at everything recorded inside this golden ocean... do they line up with your expectations?
You see it...
Ursus's inferno, Kjerag's wind and snow, Iberia's tides...
A torrent of information rushes past you, in units of civilizations, from time and space since time immemorial.
You suddenly realize—

options: Can be answered and found in this field of Originium.

steps.text: You retract your hands.

options: It is all that I've gone through that shapes what I am today.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You always have a pleasant surprise in store...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor... we managed to meet once more while I lie deep in the sea of information after our parting.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It is my past, but it is your future.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Though you might still be on a path to find yourself, you still want to prove to me that you're—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'Just as I always have been.'

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: How I wish I could see you find the answers with my own eyes. But I'm sorry... I can't go any further.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor, I have to go, and so do you all...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: If you have no intention of being trapped in this infinite nothingness for all eternity, that is.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Goodbye, Dr. {@nickname}.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: My dear friend whom I've never met.
There is no response.
The white figure atop the tower has vanished.
Nothing remains.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa... She's gone.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, what did you see?

options: What kind of person she was.
What kind of person I am.

steps.text: We'll leave this place.
The waves of information have subsided.
Do you hear the voices of the myriad souls departing, Banshee—

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The tower is at peace, Your Highness...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The waves are flowing backwards into a hell we cannot comprehend.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The flames that could burn even these roots have no way to light up the infinite night.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Where will all of you go from here?
An eternal void, a true death.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We will no longer stay on the other side, Aefanyl.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'Logos'. You should get more used to being called by this name.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You've made your choice, the choice of a Rhodes Island elite operator.
Logos stands on the endless flow of information, his own figure leaving its mark on the vast ocean.
The slender figure on the other side stands in silence.
Ripples cause her silhouette to waver, no longer clear.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: When I heard you sound the knell for yourself by the river, I was already waiting for an old friend to appear on this side.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: *sigh* A pity Laqeramaline is still unwilling to involve herself in this war.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Mother... she did indeed rescue me from death.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: With an ingenious method, but one befitting her former character.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: She has also made her choice, as you have.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I saw you confronting the myriad souls, no less impressive than the time your mother and I stood side by side in battle.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I'll have no way of seeing her again. Say farewell to her for me, Logos.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Your Highness, your figure is fading—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Departure is also a form of resistance. This is what we've chosen for ourselves.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Originium shall not cage us here for eternity.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I... don't understand. Where did the cage come from, and what do you seek for?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: There's no need to comprehend it, Logos.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You need only know the trapped myriad souls are now dissipating into freedom via a complicated flow of information impossible to parse.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No longer readable, recordable—

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'A true death'.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: All kings and heroes will no longer respond to my words, and no longer will anyone be on the other side...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Your Highness, will the myriad souls still exist after today?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Will there be ferrymen with an array on torches lighting up the other side?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No more.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Then where will our kin go, when they leave us?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I don't know... I'm afraid it's too late for me to find that answer.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I've walked to the end, and the truth of civilization lies before me in fog. There is no way for me to touch it, but it does not mean the rest of you cannot cross it.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Your Highness...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: *chuckle* I've just unloaded the burden of worrying for the future. What the myriad souls care about is only the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: 'From death comes new life'... you understand the inevitability of fate, but you have yet to clearly perceive the truth of death.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The myriad souls are no longer our shackles, and Originium will no longer be the sin we bear.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Logos, our departure also serves as our liberation.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No longer will there be prolonged indignant murmuring for a myriad years, nor an unforgettable legacy of suffering to be inherited.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: For the first time we have a future that can be changed.
'For the first time we have the right to choose.'

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: *hiss*... *huff*...

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: No surrendering here. Only death.

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: Y-You don't have to kill me...

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: Just look at the bloody crystals on my body... ugh... and my comrades... they haven't appeared from the fog...

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: I can't live on—I don't want to die—

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: Heh.
The mercenary's blade stops right before it makes contact with the dying soldier.
He looks toward the sky, and feels something leaving. The impatience to kill gradually fades away from inside him.

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: ...Gah. Did I imagine that?

steps.name: Crumbling Soldier
steps.text: *sobs*...

steps.name: Excited Mercenary
steps.text: ...Heh.
'The Sarkaz will no longer need to live for the shackles of history.'
'We will live simply for survival. Resist against suffering the exact same way as everyone else does on this land.'

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: No, my ball of yarn!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Caught you. Careful, Paprika.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Phew! Thanks! Y-You can put me down now, Ines!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We'll find a way to rescue Amiya and the rest, so don't panic.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Your life is worth more than these few balls of yarn.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: ...But my Nana gave them to me before I left home...

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Huh...? Wait, did you feel that, Ines?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Feel what?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: A pounding in the depths of your soul.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I was concentrating on the skeleton. I need to make sure it stays somewhere safe—somewhere no one can locate or affect it.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Paprika, what did it feel like exactly, and will it affect any future plans?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: I-I can't say. But... from everyone's faces, it seems like it wasn't just me!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You're... crying?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Oh, you're right! But... why?
'But what about you?'
'Me? The same as every other Sarkaz.'
'Depart. Dissipate. Die.'
'Please continue accompanying Rhodes Island on their path. There's no need to doubt your decision.'
'Thank you, Logos.'

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Your Highness, perhaps you may share my doubts on whether the myriad souls' departure will truly allow us to bid farewell to the past...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The other side will be bare, but where will the plague of death from this battlefield send the souls of our kin to?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Your Highness, I will witness our end in your stead.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The ferry is no more, so I shall guide the souls.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: If they have nowhere to go, I shall be their boat.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: My voice will set the torches on the other side aflame, and I hereby vow—

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Only when I no longer hear the roaring of my kin on the other side...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: When our compatriots can rest in peace on this land...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Will the knell cease to ring.
Ripples form on the golden water as the myriad souls respond.
Kings and heroes, regular spirits or resentful wraiths, they leave with haste.
Traces of the Sarkaz existing within Originium dissipate.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Now... please allow me to send both you and the myriad souls off.
An elegy sounds from his lips as he readies to walk over the water.
The young Banshee sends the myriad souls off.

steps.name: Sudaram
steps.text: (Indistinct Sarkaz language) ...Leave... Patriarch...

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: She is gone.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: (Ancient Sarkaz language) 'Amnannam' has bloomed, destiny already in our hands.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: She honored her vow, so the war will also abide by her.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Go, no longer shroud yourself with the fog. Water death with death, and honor departure with victory.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Victoria's condolences... I shall personally receive it in her stead.
The blue fowlbeast pecks at the tears of the white-horned demon.
She caresses the fowlbeast's feathers on its brow—Can Nightingale's inherently empty soul feel the pain of that departure?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz... did you feel that?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: The throbbing in our souls, lamenting whispers echoing in our minds.
The corners of Liz's eyes twitch minutely, unable to respond in her deep slumber.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Shining, is her condition worsening?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: No, she'll be fine.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Margaret, we have to meet with the Doctor and the others with haste.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: ...Is it because of that thing transforming in the sky earlier?

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: When it began changing, you started acting strange.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Is this another Confessarius conspiracy too?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: No... at the very least, he will be unable to involve himself in this matter for the time being.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Though it definitely has a link to his schemes.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Every Sarkaz has probably felt it—the departure of someone extremely important to us all.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: Hm... I can't fully comprehend what exactly you're talking about, but any new accidents in our current situation might affect how the war will go.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: You're right, the Doctor and the rest should have more pivotal information on their end.

steps.name: Margaret
steps.text: There's no more time to waste, let's go.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: General, General!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: This place is...

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: We were cleaning up the battlefield when we so fortunately found you...

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: General... we failed to recapture the 'Lifebone'.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Am I the only one here?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Ascalon...

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: General, your wounds...

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: We'll bring you back to camp for treatment right now.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: We missed our chance, and time is no longer on our side. Our top priority now is to return to Londinium and discuss our next move of our plan with the Regent.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Contact the spy sentries ahead to cooperate with us, and prepare to cross this warzone.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: General! Look at the blood dripping nonstop... you're in terrible shape! The Military Commission can't afford to lose another high-ranking officer!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I gave an order.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: ...This is for the remaining, living Sarkaz.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: Yes... sir.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: What happened...?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: ...Impossible. This feeling—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Your Highness, is this the price you spoke of...?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: For the Sarkaz's future...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: From today onwards, there will be no trace of your existence anywhere, even within Originium...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The 'gods', or the arrogant being professing to be the creator...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Will you see them at the end of your path... Theresa?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: After I felt you brushing past me, your voice has turned harder to hear.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: All I hear now from the void surrounding me is muffled, vapid noise.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The path ahead is clear, and it's time for everything to end.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Theresa—
'Can you still hear my voice...?'
I can.
Yours, the newborns, and the dying ones... here, we can hear the voice of every Sarkaz...
The souls are stranded in an ocean of unconsciousness, shouting our names before they drown as they await guidance.
In a present no longer recorded anywhere in time, the name we respond to the most... is 'Theresa'.
I can hear the raging rumbling from skeletons that fell from the sea of stars into the ice field ten thousand years ago. Unknown, dreadful, terrifying.
We have ended the oppression that was branded into our blood from that time onward... No, we have yet to do so.
We questioned ourselves: Did our resistance hold any meaning then?
...The future will prove it to us.
Then, what about now?
Now we shall go far, far away.
That is my reply.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The myriad souls who never gave up resisting until they completely dissipated, did one last thing for the Sarkaz within the Originium—

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: They fought for a future where everyone has a right to survive, for the ones still alive.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Onward, everyone.
That day, a certain exhausted Sarkaz girl fell into a deep sleep within the warm flames of the Kazdel Soul Furnace for some reason.
She dreamed of her mother far away in a foreign country, standing in light within the pitch-black darkness speaking to her.
She couldn't hear her clearly, but she did not cry either. Because she saw her mother smile. Then, she woke up, opened her eyes, and saw a pure white flower in full bloom by her head.
The black dust from the forge burning death landed on the fragile flower petals, but it unexpectedly highlighted the flower's dazzling vitality even more instead.
Here, death and light congregate. The girl shed tears at the beauty created by setting death aflame.
After that day, Sarkaz passing by the Soul Furnace would see a girl show up every single day to water a flower growing in the Originium dust and bones with drops of dew.
She offered tribute to the light until the day that flower withered and died.

a.text: 'Is that how the story ends...? Why is it so sad, Theresa?'
'Sad? I actually see it as a happy tale of hope arriving, Amiya.'
'The flower withered, returned to dust. But the seed of new life has already been sown.'

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: ...Did the revenant get left behind?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No, the myriad souls never took in revenants.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even if he regathers his thoughts, his intrinsically Originium-influenced self cannot be reversed or changed.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So he was never to depart with the myriad souls.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: So Her Highness never planned to take him away from here either?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have no way of knowing.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Heh... so it's not like Her Highness can't lie...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I didn't expect you to end up in my hands, old fossil.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There's no reason to harm him anymore, W.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I told you to call me Wiš'adel!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Relax, bunny. I'm not going to smash him to bits... I'm just taking him away with me.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: He already died once, so it's not hard to guess why Her Highness let him remain here.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Up 'til her death she always craved for the Sarkaz to unite, so her plan for the revenants is super simple—

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: To first live like people. Well, even if he no longer looks anything like one.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: You don't have to set everything on fire. Your mission ended a long time ago, so leave the rest to more capable people. Like me, for example...

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Bah, just stay in this weapon for the time being, yeah?

a.text: 'Do you still remember the story about the puppet, Amiya? He went into a river of tears, and sank to the riverbed...'
'Grief, despair... But it doesn't mean it's a true ending set in stone. You can always continue a story for as long as you want, but what's more important, is the storyteller.'
'The storyteller... are you talking about yourself, Theresa?'
'Me? No... Amiya, I'd prefer the storyteller be you.'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Hold on, do we have go back to where we came from to leave? Is that possible?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We won't have time. This place is changing faster than I expected.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: So what are you and the crone planning? How the hell are we leaving this place?

options: I'm still trying to figure that out!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: (Takes out explosives)

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wiš'adel! Calm down!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, I cannot tell you how to leave this place. The secrets in here are beyond even me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But I believe Theresa definitely mentioned a piece of key information to you.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: NOW WHAT?!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, Dr. Kal'tsit! These roots are breaking apart, and... floating upwards?!

a.text: 'Theresa, what if... the puppet was never alone in the first place...? Maybe his companions were waiting for him down there all along!'
'Just like us. Doctor, Dr. Kal'tsit, and you... and everyone in Babel!'
'Little people made of pebbles, white, black, green, red... a whole lot of them!'
'They'll surround the puppet and bring him far away following the fierce river waters—'
'Hm... but where can they go...?'

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We are currently 'falling' from this platform.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: 'She'... finally noticed what Theresa has done.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This tower is being erased. All the information that was organized and put together here is being broken apart.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But I can still feel Theresa's presence here, as if she still exists within the scattered information...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Everywhere, although it's vanishing quickly—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She's fighting against it... as are the myriad souls.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Get your head moving, hood! Even the platform we're on is breaking apart!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Shit! The—thing's—falling—down—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, I've got you!

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: Old hag! Your little freak isn't here to help you, so stay still, unless you wanna fall and shatter into a million pieces.

steps.name: Wiš'adel
steps.text: I have an idea on how to slow down our descent. Old fossil, get out here and help! I know you can do it!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'll wrap everyone up in my Arts too!

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The landship got swept away with the ocean waves when it was coming to a calm.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: But I remain, and I will be your ferry.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I told you, Doctor. We will reunite in peace and tranquility.

a.text: 'I got it! I know where the puppet will go, Theresa!'
'The pebble people will take the puppet along the river of tears—'
'{@nickname}.'
'Even if they get dizzy from the river's current, as long as they don't give up and stay together hand in hand...'
'They'll never get lost within the tears of sadness—'
'When you are truly confused by everything, you will remember: the answers you seek were here all along.'

spans.text: 'When you are truly confused by everything, you will remember: the answers you seek were here all along.'

options: ...I think I figured out how to leave.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Theresa, are you the one guiding us? Doctor—
You and Amiya subconsciously raise your hands at the same time.
Within the silent space, a familiar ship rises from the sea of information.
The airship that was supposedly shattered into pieces is reconstructed anew according to your intentions, hovering below you.
The both of you gaze at the giant diamond shape in the distant void...
Originium. Truth. Priestess. Theresa.
'It's time we left this place.'
The airship accelerates forward, tearing apart the void as it enters the light.

a.text: 'The puppet and his friends don't know how much time has passed, but they never give up, even though they're super tired...'
'They share the same wish, and when the water slowed down, they seized the chance to float all the way up. They succeeded, and finally they saw—'
'A sea, a golden sea painted gold by the sun.'
'It turns out they didn't just cross the river of tears, but also a vast ocean they didn't know about behind them.'
'They set foot on land once again.'
'See you, {@nickname}. I'll be here waiting for you.'

spans.text: 'See you, {@nickname}. I'll be here waiting for you.'
